Subject: Commit Amendment: Dedicated Pool Addition (16→32 GPUs) — throughput SLOs & revised reserved rate

Hi Erin —

Following our renewal check-in, thanks again for confirming Pineleaf’s interest in increasing dedicated capacity for the next term. Per our conversation last week, I’m proposing an amendment to move from your current 16-GPU reserved pool to a 32-GPU pool with a revised per-GPU reserved hourly rate and defined throughput SLOs.

High level proposal:
- Capacity: 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool) replacing current 16 GPU commitment
- Term: 12 months (aligns with current contract renewal window)
- Reserved rate (per GPU-hour): $2.45 (down from $2.80 on your existing 16-GPU commit)
- Throughput guarantee: aggregated 24/7 baseline of 240 tokens/sec across the pool with 95th percentile latency under 120ms for 512-token requests; automated fallback to compatible model variants if SLOs degrade
- Burst policy: up to 40% burst capacity above baseline for short windows (subject to autoscale cooldowns)

Attached is a cleaned amendment draft (redwood_amendment_v2.pdf) and a short throughput SLO table (throughput_slo_table.xlsx) showing expected p50/p95 performance for the models you frequently serve.

Next steps: if this direction looks good, I can loop in our contracts team for a tracked-change amendment and send a DocuSign link. If procurement wants different billing cadence or a multi-year discount, share those constraints and we’ll run numbers.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear proposal and attachments. A few clarifying questions from our side before we escalate to Procurement: 
1) The $2.45/GPU-hour rate — is that locked for the full 12-month term?
2) For the throughput guarantee, does Redwood provide credits or financial remedies if p95 latency breaches the SLO more than twice in a billing month?
3) Can you confirm that data residency and audit logs will remain the same (us-east-1, SOC2 logs retained 12 months)?

Procurement also asked for an estimate of expected monthly committed spend so they can compare to budgeting assumptions. Can you send a ballpark monthly spend for a 32-GPU reserved pool (assume 24x30 usage hours) at the proposed rate?

—Erin

Great questions — answering inline below and adding Rishi to confirm pricing/finance details.

1) Rate lock: yes, the $2.45/GPU-hour is fixed for the 12‑month committed term in the amendment. We can add language that the rate is guaranteed for the term barring mutually agreed changes.

2) Remedies: our standard SLO policy offers service credits for systemic breaches. For this amendment we propose:
- If p95 latency for covered model classes exceeds the SLO in more than 2 distinct calendar weeks in a month, customer receives a 10% credit on that month’s reserved capacity charge; if 4+ weeks then 25% credit.
- Credits are the exclusive financial remedy in the amendment; we can surface the exact language into the amendment draft.

3) Data residency & audit logs: confirmed — no change. Logs retained for 12 months (SOC2 + audit exports), and the private control plane option you already have remains available for enhanced log retention.

Monthly committed spend (ballpark): 32 GPUs * 24 hours/day * 30 days * $2.45 = $56,544/month (pre-tax). I’ll have Rishi validate if any rounding or consumption offsets apply.

If that all looks OK, I’ll start the contracts track with our legal team and send a DocuSign when ready.

Thanks,
Kimberly
